stresses: Attic R-value stated ALONE, with no depth given at all -- atticInsulation is asserted as a real number and atticInsulationDepth stays unmentioned rather than being derived/converted from the R-value (HAZARD 2b). 'Heat's a gas furnace ... forced hot air' states equipment identity and fuel but nothing about ducts-sharing-with-AC, reproducing the schema-forced hvacSystemEquipmentType axis conflation (rule 6's mechanical first-in-schema-order tie-break). A clean, unambiguous, appliance-side 'Ambient CO ... read zero' -> Passed, as a contrast case to the worked example's disclaimed personal-monitor trap -- explicitly labelled 'Ambient CO', so it is NOT an instance of the ambient-vs-undiluted-flue-CO schema confusability (RECONCILIATION.md finding). A blanket wall-insulation negation ('I can't tell you on the wall insulation') that is narrower than the whole `wall` group -- siding IS stated separately, positively, as brick veneer -- resolved per the reconciliation ruling as `group: wall`, relying on the explicit wallExteriorWallSiding leaf entry to structurally override the group disclaimer for that one leaf, rather than annotator judgment about reach.

arguable.note: SCHEMA FINDING, not a transcript ambiguity -- the same conflated-axis pattern as ANNOTATOR_GUIDE.md rule 6 / the worked example. 'Heat's a gas furnace ... forced hot air' states the equipment identity and fuel but says nothing about whether it shares ducts with a central AC unit (no AC is mentioned anywhere in this transcript). Neither 'Furnace with standalone ducts' nor 'Furnace / Central AC (shared ducts)' is more supportable than the other. `member` holds 'Furnace with standalone ducts' purely because it is FIRST in schema.ts's own enum-list order for this leaf (index 2 of 17, vs. index 16) -- the deterministic, no-discretion tie-break, not a preference.

notes.hvac.hvacHeatingSystemModelYear: 'the manufacture date stamped' on the unit's own label is read as the UNIT's model year (schema.ts: 'the UNIT's model year, e.g. 2011'), not the home's year -- this is exactly the plate-reading an auditor does to get a model year, not an inference beyond what was said.
notes.wall.wallExteriorWallSiding: SCHEMA FINDING (see RECONCILIATION.md): the pre-rebuild field set had a separate 'wallConstruction' concept ('brick veneer' over a frame wall is NOT the same as a solid-masonry 'full_brick' structural member) with no equivalent in the rebuilt 51 leaves -- there is no leaf at all for wall FRAMING/structure (2x6, full masonry, etc.), only wallExteriorWallSiding (cladding) and the cavity-insulation leaves. 'Brick Veneer' here is genuinely the siding leaf's answer, not a stand-in for a missing framing field.
notes._general: 'No gaps except right around the chimney chase where somebody left it open, I'll note that' (attic) and 'looks like they were done all at once' (windows) are both real observations with NO corresponding leaf in the 51 -- no attic leaf covers air-sealing gaps, and no window leaf covers install-timing/age. Deliberately excluded, per rule 9, rather than missed. attic.atticInsulationDepth is never stated (only the R-value is) and is therefore genuinely 'unmentioned', not declared_absent and not derived/converted from the R-value. hvac.hvacUpgradeAction (a required write field) is never addressed -- the auditor states equipment facts and says the furnace 'runs fine' but recommends no course of action -- so it stays unmentioned rather than inferred from 'runs fine'. The DHW group, all 13 health-matrix leaves besides healthAmbientCarbonMonoxide, healthRoofCondition, atticHasKneeWall, atticRoofType, and every basedata leaf besides the blower-door pair are never brought up at all (not even by a blanket negation) and are correctly absent from `leaves`.
